newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slightly up, supported by U.S. mkt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slightly up, supported by U.S. mkt.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to higher late morning Tuesday as bonds were supported by other markets in the region and by U.S. Treasuries.
"The market is looking solid," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 93-1/2 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.05 at 123.65.
"The market is just rising in line with the decline in the U.S. long bond yield," said another trader. The U.S. 30-year yield was last at 6.89 percent.
Players said activity was subdued with slim volumes capping market movments.
